name: RESTORE Colorado Program
summary: Annual NFWF grants, with Great Outdoors Colorado and other partners, for at-scale habitat restoration and stewardship in Colorado: wetlands, riparian areas, grasslands, sagebrush rangelands and migration corridors.

eligibility.rule: Is a 501(c)3, state subdivision, local government, Native Nation, Indigenous-led group or educational institution
Is not a business or unincorporated individual
Directly and measurably contributes to one or more program priorities at landscape scale
No NFWF funds for ongoing legal compliance, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlements

documents: Project maps and/or diagrams of on-site work, if applicable
Statement of litigation, unless a government applicant
Board members list, or statement that no board exists
GAAP audited financial statements, unless current valid information is already on file
IRS Form 990, unless current valid information is already on file
Single Audit, unless current valid information is already on file

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c)3 organizations, political subdivisions of the state, local and municipal governments, Native Nations and Indigenous-led organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: All projects must occur entirely within the State of Colorado.

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

window.quote: The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) is soliciting proposals for the annual Restoration and Stewardship of Outdoor Resources and Environment (RESTORE) Colorado Program.

amount.quote: with a minimum grant amount of $100,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Due to the combination of federal, state, and private funding sources involved in the RESTORE Colorado Program, leverage and match are encouraged but not required.

effort.quote: Once an application has been initiated, it may be saved and then modified and submitted at a later time, up to the application deadline of November 12, 2026 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time.

eligibility.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c)3 organizations, political subdivisions of the state, local and municipal governments, Native Nations and Indigenous-led organizations, and educational institutions.
Ineligible applicants include businesses and unincorporated individuals.
All projects must occur entirely within the State of Colorado.
All proposals must specifically address how projects will directly and measurably contribute to the landscape-scale accomplishment of one or more of the program priorities described below.
NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements.

documents.quote: Full Proposal Narrative: The most important upload is your actual full proposal narrative.
